hints: List the SI base units in this question: $v$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$, $g$ in $\text{m s}^{-2}$ and $L$ in $\text{m}$, with $2\pi$ having no units.
Combine $g$ and $L$ to see that the product $gL$ has units $\text{m}^2 \text{ s}^{-2}$, so a square root is needed to get $\text{m s}^{-1}$.

Test each option by checking whether the $g$ and $L$ combination gives $\text{m s}^{-1}$ after any square root, and reject the ones giving $\text{m}^2 \text{ s}^{-2}$, $\text{s}^{-1}$ or $\text{s}^{-2}$.
walkthrough: Identify the required units: $v$ must have units of speed, $\text{m s}^{-1}$, while $g$ is $\text{m s}^{-2}$ and $L$ is $\text{m}$.
State the homogeneity rule: both sides of a possible physics equation must have the same units, and constants such as $2\pi$ are dimensionless.
Check the combination $gL$: $[gL] = (\text{m s}^{-2})(\text{m}) = \text{m}^2 \text{ s}^{-2}$, so $\sqrt{gL}$ gives $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
Apply this to option A: $\left[\sqrt{gL/2\pi}\right] = \sqrt{\text{m}^2 \text{ s}^{-2}} = \text{m s}^{-1}$, which matches $v$.
Eliminate the others: option B gives $\text{m}^2 \text{ s}^{-2}$, option C gives $\sqrt{\text{s}^{-2}} = \text{s}^{-1}$, and option D gives $\text{s}^{-2}$, so none matches $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
Therefore only the square root of $gL$ divided by $2\pi$ is homogeneous. This is option A

A.explanation: Inside the square root, $gL$ has units $\text{m}^2 \text{ s}^{-2}$, so $\sqrt{gL/2\pi}$ has units $\text{m s}^{-1}$, matching $v$.

B.explanation: $gL$ has units $\text{m}^2 \text{ s}^{-2}$, so $gL/4\pi^2$ does not have the units $\text{m s}^{-1}$ required for speed.

C.explanation: $g/L$ has units $\text{s}^{-2}$, so $\sqrt{g/L}$ has units $\text{s}^{-1}$, which is a frequency unit not a speed.

D.explanation: $g/L$ has units $\text{s}^{-2}$, so $2\pi g/L$ has units $\text{s}^{-2}$ and cannot equal speed $v$.
